15"""Registration table for the multi-input ``aten::_foreach_*`` family. 

16 

17Twelve operators with four overload shapes each share the multi-input executor 

18in :mod:`flag_gems.utils.foreach`. As in :mod:`flag_gems.ops._foreach_unary`, 

19every operator is a table row rather than a copy of the wrapper; what differs 

20between rows is only the element-wise math and the accepted dtypes. 

21 

22Two facts about this family, measured against the pinned PyTorch build rather 

23than inferred from the names: 

24 

25* ``_foreach_add`` and friends have **no** ``default`` overload -- only 

26 ``Scalar`` / ``List`` / ``ScalarList`` / ``Tensor``. Registering the bare 

27 name would never dispatch and would raise no error (CLAUDE.md 7.1 class B), 

28 so each overload is registered under its full name. 

29* The ``.Tensor`` overload broadcasts *one* tensor across the whole list, while 

30 ``.List`` pairs the two lists position by position. They are different 

31 operations and get different wrappers. 

32 

33The ``.out`` overloads are deliberately absent: for this family they decompose 

34to the functional form, so registering them would add keys that are never 

35consulted. Verified by calling ``torch.ops.aten._foreach_sqrt.out`` and 

36observing the functional kernel's debug record. 

37""" 

38

74# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- 

75# element-wise math 

76# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- 

77# 

78# These are written here rather than borrowed from the single-tensor operators 

79# because those carry extra machinery the executor cannot use: ``add_func`` 

80# takes an ``alpha`` argument bound by ``pointwise_dynamic``, and several of 

81# them cast to ``float32`` internally, which would silently change the result 

82# dtype of an integer foreach call. Each function below is the bare two- or 

83# three-argument form the executor's ``tl.constexpr`` slot expects. 

84 

85 

86@triton.jit 

87def _add_fn(a, b): 

88 # The paired kernel hands over the raw int1 operand, and arithmetic on int1 

89 # in this Triton backend behaves like ``and`` (``True + True`` is False). 

90 # ATen defines bool addition as logical or, so the operand is combined 

91 # explicitly instead. 

92 if a.dtype == tl.int1: 

93 return a | b 

94 return a + b 

95 

96 

97@triton.jit 

98def _sub_fn(a, b): 

99 return a - b 

100 

101 

102@triton.jit 

103def _mul_fn(a, b): 

104 # Multiplication on int1 already coincides with logical and, but the operand 

105 # is combined explicitly so the bool path does not depend on that. 

106 if a.dtype == tl.int1: 

107 return a & b 

108 return a * b 

109 

110 

111@triton.jit 

112def _div_fn(a, b): 

113 return a / b 

114 

115 

116@triton.jit 

117def _maximum_fn(a, b): 

118 return tl.maximum(a, b) 

119 

120 

121@triton.jit 

122def _minimum_fn(a, b): 

123 return tl.minimum(a, b) 

124 

125 

126@triton.jit 

127def _pow_fn(a, b): 

128 # The shim's ``pow`` needs floating point operands; integral foreach pow is 

129 # promoted by the executor before the call, so the cast here only affects 

130 # the intermediate and not the stored dtype. A bool base takes the same 

131 # path: ATen computes ``bool ** float`` in floating point (``False ** -1`` 

132 # is ``inf``), which the plain power already gives once the operand is 

133 # promoted. 

134 af = a.to(tl.float32) 

135 bf = b.to(tl.float32) 

136 if _FAST_MATH and (a.dtype == tl.float16 or a.dtype == tl.bfloat16): 

137 # 16-bit output: ``powf`` is about half the kernel time, and the 

138 # fixups a negative base needs are exactly what a *block-wide* guard 

139 # would avoid -- but on data with mixed signs that guard never fires 

140 # (one negative base rejects the whole block), so the full ``powf`` 

141 # runs on every element. Pay for the closed form per element 

142 # instead, cheap enough that the guard is not worth keeping: 

143 # 

144 # |a| ** b = exp2(fast_log2f(|a|) * b) 

145 # 

146 # and supply the sign separately: a negative base is ``(-1)**b`` for 

147 # an integral ``b`` and NaN otherwise. The 16-bit output tolerance 

148 # (fp16 rtol 1e-3, bf16 0.016) absorbs the ~2**-22 relative error of 

149 # ``lg2.approx``; fp32/fp64 keep the exact path below bit for bit, so 

150 # their ltol 1.3e-6 result is unchanged. 

151 s = tl.abs(af) 

152 if a.dtype == tl.bfloat16: 

153 # A bf16 subnormal *is* an fp32 subnormal, and ``lg2.approx`` 

154 # flushes those to zero (``pow(2**-133, -0.5)`` would come back 

155 # inf). Scale them into the normal range first; the scale is a 

156 # power of two, so the multiply is exact and the logarithm only 

157 # shifts by a constant. fp16 subnormals are normal in fp32 and 

158 # skip this. 

159 sub = s < 1.1754943508222875e-38 

160 lg = tl_extra_shim.fast_log2f(tl.where(sub, s * 16777216.0, s)) - tl.where( 

161 sub, 24.0, 0.0 

162 ) 

163 else: 

164 lg = tl_extra_shim.fast_log2f(s) 

165 # ``|a| == 1`` is pinned to 1: the magnitude is 1 for every exponent, 

166 # while ``exp2(0 * inf)`` is NaN and ``pow(±1, ±inf)`` is 1. 

167 r = tl.where(s == 1.0, 1.0, tl.exp2(lg * bf)) 

168 # Negative base: ``(-1)**b`` when ``b`` is integral, NaN otherwise. 

169 # Parity is tested through ``b/2`` because ``bi % 2`` is exact only for 

170 # ``|b| < 2**24``; ``b == 2**24`` is even and ``2**24 - 1`` is odd, and 

171 # ``floor`` keeps both halves of the test on representable values. 

172 bi = tl.floor(bf) 

173 odd = (bi * 0.5) != tl.floor(bi * 0.5) 

174 # ``signbit`` rather than ``af < 0`` so that ``-0.0`` counts as 

175 # negative: ``pow(-0.0, -1)`` is ``-inf``, not ``+inf``. 

176 neg = tl_extra_shim.signbit(af) != 0 

177 r = tl.where( 

178 neg, 

179 tl.where( 

180 bf == bi, 

181 tl.where(odd, -r, r), 

182 # A zero or infinite magnitude is never NaN however fractional 

183 # ``b`` is: ATen gives ``pow(-0.0, 0.5) == -0.0`` and 

184 # ``pow(-inf, 0.5) == inf``, and ``exp2`` of ``-inf * b`` / 

185 # ``inf * b`` already produces the right 0 or inf. 

186 tl.where((s == 0.0) | (s == float("inf")), r, float("nan")), 

187 ), 

188 r, 

189 ) 

190 # ``b == 0`` is pinned to 1 because ``exp2(-inf * 0)`` is NaN while 

191 # ``pow(0, 0)`` and ``pow(nan, 0)`` are 1. 

192 r = tl.where(bf == 0.0, 1.0, r) 

193 elif a.dtype.is_floating(): 

194 # ``powf`` dominates the kernel time and is itself ``exp2(y * log2 x)`` 

195 # plus the fixups a negative base needs. On a block of normal, positive 

196 # bases those fixups are dead code, so evaluate the cheap form instead. 

197 # The guard is a block-wide ``tl.min`` (one reduction per program); a 

198 # per-element ``tl.where`` executes both branches and measured 35-60% 

199 # slower than the plain power. The bound is the smallest normal fp32: 

200 # a subnormal base stays > 0 but ``log2`` flushes it to zero, and 

201 # ``pow(2**-149, -0.5)`` came back as ``2.7e22`` instead of ``1.3e19`` 

202 # (rel 2.0e3) when the fast path was allowed to see it. 

203 # ``a == 1`` is pinned to 1 because ``exp2(log2(1) * inf)`` is NaN while 

204 # ``pow(1, inf)`` is 1; ``b == 0`` is pinned for the same reason on an 

205 # infinite base (``exp2(inf * 0)`` is NaN, ``pow(inf, 0)`` is 1). 

206 if tl.min(af) >= 1.1754943508222875e-38: 

207 r = tl.where((af == 1.0) | (bf == 0.0), 1.0, tl.exp2(tl.log2(af) * bf)) 

208 else: 

209 r = _pow(af, bf) 

210 else: 

211 # Integral results use ``powf`` unchanged: the last-bit difference 

212 # changes the value once truncated to an integer. 

213 r = _pow(af, bf) 

214 return r 

215 

216 

217@triton.jit 

218def _rpow_fn(a, b): 

219 # ``pow.ScalarAndTensor``: the scalar is the base, so the power is reversed 

220 # relative to ``_pow_fn`` (``a`` is the exponent, ``b`` the base). Kept at 

221 # module scope like every other kernel: defining it inside the wrapper 

222 # rebuilt the ``JITFunction`` and its caches on every call. 

223 af = a.to(tl.float32) 

224 bf = b.to(tl.float32) 

225 # Same positive-base fast path as ``_pow_fn``. The base is the scalar 

226 # here, so the guard is the scalar condition itself -- ``tl.min`` rejects 

227 # a 0-d operand in this Triton. The smallest-normal bound and the 

228 # ``exponent == 0`` pin carry over unchanged. 

229 if b.dtype.is_floating(): 

230 if bf >= 1.1754943508222875e-38: 

231 r = tl.where((bf == 1.0) | (af == 0.0), 1.0, tl.exp2(tl.log2(bf) * af)) 

232 else: 

233 r = _pow(bf, af) 

234 else: 

235 r = _pow(bf, af) 

236 return r

239@triton.jit 

240def _copy_fn(a, b): 

241 # ``_foreach_copy`` overwrites self with src; the first operand is read and 

242 # discarded so the executor's paired addressing still applies. 

243 return b

246@triton.jit 

247def _lerp_tensor_weight_fn(a, b, w, _unused): 

248 # ``lerp.List``: the weight is the third tensor operand. 

249 return a + w * (b - a) 

250 

251 

252@triton.jit 

253def _lerp_scalar_weight_fn(a, b, _c, w): 

254 # ``lerp.Scalar`` / ``.ScalarList``: the weight arrives as the scalar; the 

255 # third tensor slot is a copy of ``b`` and is ignored. 

256 return a + w * (b - a) 

257 

258 

259@triton.jit 

260def _addcmul_fn(a, b, c, v): 

261 return a + v * b * c 

262 

263 

264@triton.jit 

265def _addcdiv_fn(a, b, c, v): 

266 return a + v * (b / c)

269# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- 

270# GCU400 flat launches for the grid.y hardware cap 

271# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- 

272# 

273# The common paired/ternary executors launch on the 2D grid 

274# ``(nt, cdiv(max_numel, BLOCK))``, and GCU400 caps ``grid.y`` at 255: a 

275# uniform float group whose largest tensor needs 256+ tiles -- sixteen 512^2 

276# fp32 tensors at ``BLOCK=1024`` is exactly 256 -- raises ``OutOfResources`` 

277# at launch and the operator aborts. The scalar overloads already run on the 

278# grid-stride kernel in ``utils/foreach.py`` (axis 1 capped at 

279# ``MAX_GRID_DIM``); the two kernels below extend that scheme to the paired 

280# and ternary bodies, and the ``_flat_*`` hosts replay the common executors' 

281# uniform-list semantics in front of them. 

282# 

283# A flat path is taken *only* when the common launch would exceed the 

284# hardware limits, so every shape that fits keeps the common executors and 

285# their tuned launch caches untouched. Anything the flat host cannot serve 

286# exactly -- mixed dtypes, non-contiguous or overlapping views, integral or 

287# bool operands, heterogeneous output dtypes -- also answers 

288# ``_FLAT_FALLBACK`` and keeps the common error wording. 

289 

290_FLAT_FALLBACK = object() 

291 

292_MAX_GRID_X = 65535 

293_MAX_GRID_Y = 255 

294 

295_FLAT_FLOAT = (torch.float16, torch.float32, torch.bfloat16) 

296 

297 

298@triton.jit 

299def _foreach_binary_flat_kernel( 

300 meta_ptr, 

301 fn: tl.constexpr, 

302 NT: tl.constexpr, 

303 A_DT: tl.constexpr, 

304 B_DT: tl.constexpr, 

305 OUT_DT: tl.constexpr, 

306 ALPHA: tl.constexpr, 

307 B_SCALAR: tl.constexpr, 

308 BLOCK: tl.constexpr, 

309 NCTA, 

310): 

311 """Paired-list math on a grid-stride ``(NT, NCTA)`` launch. 

312 

313 The metadata layout matches the common ``foreach_binary_kernel``: 

314 first-input, second-input and output pointers plus element counts, ``NT`` 

315 each, int64. Axis 1 carries at most ``NCTA`` starting tiles and each 

316 program strides over the remaining ones, so the second axis never grows 

317 past the GCU400 limit no matter how large the tensors are. 

318 """ 

319 tensor_id = tl.program_id(0) 

320 tile_id = tl.program_id(1) 

321 

322 a_ptr = tl.load(meta_ptr + tensor_id).to(tl.pointer_type(A_DT)) 

323 b_ptr = tl.load(meta_ptr + NT + tensor_id).to(tl.pointer_type(B_DT)) 

324 out_ptr = tl.load(meta_ptr + 2 * NT + tensor_id).to(tl.pointer_type(OUT_DT)) 

325 n_elements = tl.load(meta_ptr + 3 * NT + tensor_id) 

326 

327 num_tiles = tl.cdiv(n_elements, BLOCK).to(tl.int32) 

328 for block_id in tl.range(tile_id, num_tiles, NCTA): 

329 idx = block_id * BLOCK + tl.arange(0, BLOCK) 

330 mask = idx < n_elements 

331 a = tl.load(a_ptr + idx, mask=mask, other=0) 

332 if B_SCALAR: 

333 b = tl.load(b_ptr) 

334 else: 

335 b = tl.load(b_ptr + idx, mask=mask, other=0) 

336 b = (b * ALPHA).to(OUT_DT) if ALPHA != 1 else b.to(OUT_DT) 

337 tl.store(out_ptr + idx, fn(a.to(OUT_DT), b).to(OUT_DT), mask=mask) 

338 

339 

340@triton.jit 

341def _foreach_ternary_flat_kernel( 

342 meta_ptr, 

343 scalar_ptr, 

344 fn: tl.constexpr, 

345 NT: tl.constexpr, 

346 A_DT: tl.constexpr, 

347 OUT_DT: tl.constexpr, 

348 S_DT: tl.constexpr, 

349 BLOCK: tl.constexpr, 

350 NCTA, 

351): 

352 """Ternary-list math on a grid-stride ``(NT, NCTA)`` launch. 

353 

354 The metadata layout matches the common ``foreach_ternary_kernel``: 

355 self, tensor1 and tensor2 pointers, output pointers and element counts, 

356 ``NT`` each, int64; ``scalar_ptr`` holds one value per tensor. The 

357 scalars ride in a device array of the output dtype rather than a 

358 by-value ``float64`` argument, keeping the signature f64-free exactly 

359 like the GCU400 scalar executor. 

360 """ 

361 tensor_id = tl.program_id(0) 

362 tile_id = tl.program_id(1) 

363 

364 a_ptr = tl.load(meta_ptr + tensor_id).to(tl.pointer_type(A_DT)) 

365 b_ptr = tl.load(meta_ptr + NT + tensor_id).to(tl.pointer_type(A_DT)) 

366 c_ptr = tl.load(meta_ptr + 2 * NT + tensor_id).to(tl.pointer_type(A_DT)) 

367 out_ptr = tl.load(meta_ptr + 3 * NT + tensor_id).to(tl.pointer_type(OUT_DT)) 

368 n_elements = tl.load(meta_ptr + 4 * NT + tensor_id) 

369 s = tl.load(scalar_ptr + tensor_id) 

370 

371 num_tiles = tl.cdiv(n_elements, BLOCK).to(tl.int32) 

372 for block_id in tl.range(tile_id, num_tiles, NCTA): 

373 idx = block_id * BLOCK + tl.arange(0, BLOCK) 

374 mask = idx < n_elements 

375 a = tl.load(a_ptr + idx, mask=mask, other=0).to(OUT_DT) 

376 b = tl.load(b_ptr + idx, mask=mask, other=0).to(OUT_DT) 

377 c = tl.load(c_ptr + idx, mask=mask, other=0).to(OUT_DT) 

378 tl.store(out_ptr + idx, fn(a, b, c, s.to(OUT_DT)).to(OUT_DT), mask=mask) 

379 

380 

381def _common_grid_overflows(numels) -> bool: 

382 """Whether the common paired launch grid exceeds the GCU400 limits. 

383 

384 The paired executor launches ``(nt, cdiv(max_numel, BLOCK))`` with the 

385 ``BLOCK`` its own search picks, so the answer is computed the same way; 

386 ``True`` means the launch would raise ``OutOfResources`` on grid.y. 

387 """ 

388 nt = len(numels) 

389 max_numel = max(numels) 

390 if nt == 0 or max_numel == 0: 

391 return False 

392 block = _pick_block(numels) 

393 tiles = -(-max_numel // block) 

394 return nt > _MAX_GRID_X or tiles > _MAX_GRID_Y 

395 

396 

397def _common_ternary_grid_overflows(numels, dtype, values) -> bool: 

398 """Whether the common ternary launch grid exceeds the GCU400 limits. 

399 

400 The ternary launcher transposes its grid for the packed 16-bit kernel 

401 above ``2**20`` elements, which hides the tile count on axis 0; every 

402 other launch puts it on axis 1 where the 255 cap bites. ``values`` is 

403 the pointer/numel run the launch would upload, for the same pack test 

404 the common launcher applies. 

405 """ 

406 nt = len(numels) 

407 max_numel = max(numels) 

408 if nt == 0 or max_numel == 0: 

409 return False 

410 block = _pick_block(numels) 

411 tiles = -(-max_numel // block) 

412 swap = ( 

413 _pack_ok((dtype, dtype), max_numel, values) 

414 and max_numel >= _TERNARY_SWAP_MIN_ELEMS 

415 ) 

416 if swap: 

417 return tiles > _MAX_GRID_X or nt > _MAX_GRID_Y 

418 return nt > _MAX_GRID_X or tiles > _MAX_GRID_Y 

419

421def _flat_binary_list( 

422 self, 

423 other, 

424 fn, 

425 *, 

426 inplace=False, 

427 alpha=1, 

428 allowed_dtypes=None, 

429 out_dtype_fn=None, 

430 out_dtypes=None, 

431 copy_semantics=False, 

432 scalar_operand=False, 

433): 

434 """Uniform float paired lists on the flat kernel, or ``_FLAT_FALLBACK``. 

435 

436 Replays the common executor's uniform-list semantics -- dtype refusal, 

437 promotion, allocation and the in-place pairing -- for exactly the groups 

438 whose common launch would exceed the GCU400 grid limits. Every other 

439 shape answers ``_FLAT_FALLBACK`` and the caller hands it to the common 

440 executor unchanged, error wording included. 

441 """ 

442 if not isinstance(self, (list, tuple)) or not self: 

443 return _FLAT_FALLBACK 

444 nt = len(self) 

445 if not isinstance(other, (list, tuple)) or len(other) != nt: 

446 return _FLAT_FALLBACK 

447 if nt > _MAX_GRID_X: 

448 return _FLAT_FALLBACK 

449 a0 = self[0] 

450 if not isinstance(a0, torch.Tensor): 

451 return _FLAT_FALLBACK 

452 if not all(isinstance(t, torch.Tensor) for t in self): 

453 return _FLAT_FALLBACK 

454 device = a0.device 

455 a_dt = a0.dtype 

456 if a_dt not in _FLAT_FLOAT: 

457 return _FLAT_FALLBACK 

458 if allowed_dtypes is not None and a_dt not in allowed_dtypes: 

459 return _FLAT_FALLBACK 

460 numels = [t.numel() for t in self] 

461 if not _common_grid_overflows(numels): 

462 return _FLAT_FALLBACK 

463 

464 b0 = other[0] 

465 if not isinstance(b0, torch.Tensor): 

466 return _FLAT_FALLBACK 

467 b_dt = b0.dtype 

468 if b_dt not in _FLAT_FLOAT: 

469 return _FLAT_FALLBACK 

470 a_zero_dim = a0.dim() == 0 

471 for t in self: 

472 if ( 

473 t.dtype is not a_dt 

474 or t.device != device 

475 or not t.is_contiguous() 

476 or (t.dim() == 0) != a_zero_dim 

477 ): 

478 return _FLAT_FALLBACK 

479 if scalar_operand: 

480 if b0.device != device or not b0.is_contiguous(): 

481 return _FLAT_FALLBACK 

482 else: 

483 b_zero_dim = b0.dim() == 0 

484 for t in other: 

485 if ( 

486 t.dtype is not b_dt 

487 or t.device != device 

488 or not t.is_contiguous() 

489 or (t.dim() == 0) != b_zero_dim 

490 ): 

491 return _FLAT_FALLBACK 

492 

493 if out_dtypes is not None: 

494 out_dt = out_dtypes[0] 

495 if any(dt is not out_dt for dt in out_dtypes): 

496 return _FLAT_FALLBACK 

497 elif copy_semantics: 

498 out_dt = a_dt 

499 elif b_dt is a_dt: 

500 out_dt = a_dt 

501 else: 

502 out_dt = _promote_dtypes(a0, b0) 

503 if out_dtypes is None and not copy_semantics and out_dtype_fn is not None: 

504 out_dt = out_dtype_fn(out_dt) 

505 if out_dt not in _FLAT_FLOAT: 

506 return _FLAT_FALLBACK 

507 if inplace and out_dt is not a_dt: 

508 return _FLAT_FALLBACK 

509 

510 _STATS.reset() 

511 if inplace: 

512 results = list(self) 

513 elif out_dt is a_dt: 

514 results = list(map(torch.empty_like, self)) 

515 else: 

516 results = [torch.empty_like(t, dtype=out_dt) for t in self] 

517 

518 a_ptrs = [t.data_ptr() for t in self] 

519 if scalar_operand: 

520 b_ptrs = [b0.data_ptr()] * nt 

521 else: 

522 b_ptrs = [t.data_ptr() for t in other] 

523 out_ptrs = a_ptrs if inplace else [t.data_ptr() for t in results] 

524 meta = _device_meta(a_ptrs + b_ptrs + out_ptrs + numels, device) 

525 

526 block = _pick_block(numels) 

527 tiles = -(-max(numels) // block) 

528 ncta = min(tiles, MAX_GRID_DIM) 

529 _foreach_binary_flat_kernel[(nt, ncta)]( 

530 meta, 

531 fn, 

532 nt, 

533 tl_dtype(a_dt), 

534 tl_dtype(b_dt), 

535 tl_dtype(out_dt), 

536 alpha, 

537 scalar_operand, 

538 block, 

539 ncta, 

540 num_warps=4, 

541 ) 

542 _STATS.executor_launches += 1 

543 _STATS.groups += 1 

544 return results 

545 

546 

547def _flat_ternary( 

548 self, 

549 tensor1, 

550 tensor2, 

551 scalars, 

552 fn, 

553 *, 

554 inplace=False, 

555 allowed_dtypes=None, 

556): 

557 """Uniform float ternary lists on the flat kernel, or ``_FLAT_FALLBACK``. 

558 

559 The counterpart of :func:`_flat_binary_list` for the ``addcmul`` / 

560 ``addcdiv`` / ``lerp`` shapes the common ternary executor serves. The 

561 uniform-list semantics it replays are the ones of that executor's 

562 homogeneous path: one floating dtype, one device, all dense. 

563 """ 

564 if not isinstance(self, (list, tuple)) or not self: 

565 return _FLAT_FALLBACK 

566 if not isinstance(tensor1, (list, tuple)) or not isinstance(tensor2, (list, tuple)): 

567 return _FLAT_FALLBACK 

568 nt = len(self) 

569 if len(tensor1) != nt or len(tensor2) != nt: 

570 return _FLAT_FALLBACK 

571 if nt > _MAX_GRID_X: 

572 return _FLAT_FALLBACK 

573 a0 = self[0] 

574 if not isinstance(a0, torch.Tensor): 

575 return _FLAT_FALLBACK 

576 if not all(isinstance(t, torch.Tensor) for t in self): 

577 return _FLAT_FALLBACK 

578 if not all(isinstance(t, torch.Tensor) for t in tensor1): 

579 return _FLAT_FALLBACK 

580 same_bc = tensor1 is tensor2 

581 if not same_bc and not all(isinstance(t, torch.Tensor) for t in tensor2): 

582 return _FLAT_FALLBACK 

583 device = a0.device 

584 dtype = a0.dtype 

585 if dtype not in _FLAT_FLOAT: 

586 return _FLAT_FALLBACK 

587 if allowed_dtypes is not None and dtype not in allowed_dtypes: 

588 return _FLAT_FALLBACK 

589 for t in self: 

590 if t.dtype is not dtype or t.device != device or not t.is_contiguous(): 

591 return _FLAT_FALLBACK 

592 for t in tensor1: 

593 if t.dtype is not dtype or t.device != device or not t.is_contiguous(): 

594 return _FLAT_FALLBACK 

595 if not same_bc: 

596 for t in tensor2: 

597 if t.dtype is not dtype or t.device != device or not t.is_contiguous(): 

598 return _FLAT_FALLBACK 

599 try: 

600 values, _, _ = _resolve_scalars(self, scalars) 

601 except Exception: 

602 return _FLAT_FALLBACK 

603 if not all(isinstance(v, (int, float)) for v in values): 

604 return _FLAT_FALLBACK 

605 

606 a_ptrs = [t.data_ptr() for t in self] 

607 b_ptrs = [t.data_ptr() for t in tensor1] 

608 c_ptrs = b_ptrs if same_bc else [t.data_ptr() for t in tensor2] 

609 numels = [t.numel() for t in self] 

610 # The pack test reads alignment off the whole pointer run; for the 

611 # out-of-place form the freshly allocated destinations are at least as 

612 # aligned as the inputs, so the inputs answer the same question. 

613 if not _common_ternary_grid_overflows( 

614 numels, dtype, a_ptrs + b_ptrs + c_ptrs + a_ptrs + numels 

615 ): 

616 return _FLAT_FALLBACK 

617 

618 _STATS.reset() 

619 if inplace: 

620 results = list(self) 

621 out_ptrs = a_ptrs 

622 else: 

623 results = list(map(torch.empty_like, self)) 

624 out_ptrs = [t.data_ptr() for t in results] 

625 meta = _device_meta(a_ptrs + b_ptrs + c_ptrs + out_ptrs + numels, device) 

626 scalar_buf = torch.tensor([float(v) for v in values], dtype=dtype).to( 

627 device, non_blocking=True 

628 ) 

629 

630 block = _pick_block(numels) 

631 tiles = -(-max(numels) // block) 

632 ncta = min(tiles, MAX_GRID_DIM) 

633 _foreach_ternary_flat_kernel[(nt, ncta)]( 

634 meta, 

635 scalar_buf, 

636 fn, 

637 nt, 

638 tl_dtype(dtype), 

639 tl_dtype(dtype), 

640 tl_dtype(dtype), 

641 block, 

642 ncta, 

643 num_warps=4, 

644 ) 

645 _STATS.executor_launches += 1 

646 _STATS.groups += 1 

647 return results 

648 

649 

650# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- 

651# dtype sets, as measured 

652# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- 

653 

654_FLOAT = (torch.float16, torch.bfloat16, torch.float32, torch.float64) 

655_INT = (torch.int8, torch.int16, torch.int32, torch.int64, torch.uint8) 

656 

657# Arithmetic accepts bool as well; the comparison-style clamps do not reject it 

658# either. Complex is excluded here because the paired kernels have no 

659# interleaved-component path (the unary executor's complex support does not 

660# generalise to two operands). 

661ARITH = frozenset(_FLOAT + _INT + (torch.bool,)) 

662# ``lerp`` / ``addcdiv`` are floating point only: an integral lerp would need to 

663# round the interpolation, and ATen refuses instead. 

664FLOAT_ONLY = frozenset(_FLOAT) 

665 

666# bool support is per *operator*, not per family, and two of the exceptions 

667# depend on the overload of the second operand: ATen defines bool addition as 

668# logical or but refuses ``bool - bool`` outright, and the clamp family accepts 

669# a bool tensor operand yet rejects a bool scalar one. 

670NO_BOOL = frozenset(_FLOAT + _INT) 

671# ``pow`` has no bool kernel in the .List form but the .Scalar / .ScalarList 

672# forms do accept it. ATen reports it as NotImplementedError, not a dtype error. 

673_POW_BOOL_ERROR = "\"pow\" not implemented for 'Bool'" 

674 

675 

676def _float_result(dtype: torch.dtype) -> torch.dtype: 

677 """Promote an integral result to the default float type. 

678 

679 ``_foreach_div`` on integers returns float, matching ``torch.div``'s true 

680 division; the executor asks for this through ``out_dtype_fn``. 

681 """ 

682 if dtype.is_floating_point or dtype.is_complex: 

683 return dtype 

684 return torch.float32 

685 

686 

687class BinaryOp: 

688 """One row of the multi-input foreach table.""" 

689 

690 __slots__ = ( 

691 "name", 

692 "fn", 

693 "allowed", 

694 "allowed_scalar", 

695 "dtype_error", 

696 "dtype_error_type", 

697 "out_dtype_fn", 

698 "arity", 

699 ) 

700 

701 def __init__( 

702 self, 

703 name: str, 

704 fn: Callable, 

705 allowed: Optional[frozenset] = ARITH, 

706 out_dtype_fn: Optional[Callable] = None, 

707 arity: int = 2, 

708 allowed_scalar: Optional[frozenset] = None, 

709 dtype_error: Optional[str] = None, 

710 dtype_error_type: type = RuntimeError, 

711 ) -> None: 

712 self.name = name 

713 self.fn = fn 

714 self.allowed = allowed 

715 # The .Scalar / .ScalarList overloads sometimes accept a narrower set 

716 # than .List; ``None`` means "same as ``allowed``". 

717 self.allowed_scalar = allowed_scalar 

718 # Replaces the generic dtype text when ATen words the refusal 

719 # differently for this operator. 

720 self.dtype_error = dtype_error 

721 self.dtype_error_type = dtype_error_type 

722 self.out_dtype_fn = out_dtype_fn 

723 self.arity = arity 

724 

725 

726# ATen's own wording for the one operator that refuses bool with a dedicated 

727# message rather than the generic "not implemented" text. 

728_SUB_BOOL_ERROR = ( 

729 "Subtraction, the `-` operator, with two bool tensors is not supported. " 

730 "Use the `^` or `logical_xor()` operator instead." 

731) 

732 

733 

734BINARY_OPS: Dict[str, BinaryOp] = { 

735 op.name: op 

736 for op in ( 

737 BinaryOp("add", _add_fn), 

738 # ATen refuses ``bool - bool`` rather than defining it. 

739 BinaryOp("sub", _sub_fn, NO_BOOL, dtype_error=_SUB_BOOL_ERROR), 

740 BinaryOp("mul", _mul_fn), 

741 BinaryOp("div", _div_fn, ARITH, _float_result), 

742 BinaryOp("clamp_max", _minimum_fn, allowed_scalar=NO_BOOL), 

743 BinaryOp("clamp_min", _maximum_fn, allowed_scalar=NO_BOOL), 

744 BinaryOp("maximum", _maximum_fn, allowed_scalar=NO_BOOL), 

745 BinaryOp("minimum", _minimum_fn, allowed_scalar=NO_BOOL), 

746 # ``pow`` rejects a bool tensor operand but accepts a bool scalar; the 

747 # refusal is NotImplementedError in ATen rather than a dtype error. 

748 # Its result dtype is plain ``result_type(base, exponent)``, so unlike 

749 # ``div`` it needs no output-dtype callback. 

750 BinaryOp( 

751 "pow", 

752 _pow_fn, 

753 NO_BOOL, 

754 allowed_scalar=ARITH, 

755 dtype_error=_POW_BOOL_ERROR, 

756 dtype_error_type=NotImplementedError, 

757 ), 

758 # ``copy`` casts the operand into the destination dtype, so every dtype 

759 # is accepted; no promotion happens. 

760 BinaryOp("copy", _copy_fn, None), 

761 BinaryOp("lerp", _lerp_tensor_weight_fn, FLOAT_ONLY, None, 3), 

762 BinaryOp("addcmul", _addcmul_fn, ARITH, None, 4), 

763 BinaryOp("addcdiv", _addcdiv_fn, FLOAT_ONLY, None, 4), 

764 ) 

765} 

766 

767 

768def _log(name: str, overload: str, inplace: bool) -> None: 

769 logger.debug( 

770 "GEMS_ENFLAME_GCU400 _FOREACH_%s%s", name.upper(), "_" if inplace else "" 

771 ) 

772 del overload 

773 

774 

775def _check_alpha(alpha, dtype: torch.dtype) -> None: 

776 """ATen refuses a fractional ``alpha`` for integral and bool operands.""" 

777 if dtype in _INT + (torch.bool,) and float(alpha) != int(alpha): 

778 raise RuntimeError( 

779 "For integral input tensors, argument alpha must not be " 

780 "a floating point number." 

781 ) 

782 

783 

784def _apply_list(name: str, self, other, inplace: bool, alpha=1): 

785 """The ``.List`` overload: pair the two lists position by position.""" 

786 op = BINARY_OPS[name] 

787 _log(name, "List", inplace) 

788 if alpha != 1: 

789 for t in self: 

790 _check_alpha(alpha, t.dtype) 

791 res = _flat_binary_list( 

792 self, 

793 other, 

794 op.fn, 

795 inplace=inplace, 

796 alpha=alpha, 

797 allowed_dtypes=op.allowed, 

798 out_dtype_fn=op.out_dtype_fn, 

799 ) 

800 if res is _FLAT_FALLBACK: 

801 res = foreach_binary_list( 

802 self, 

803 other, 

804 op.fn, 

805 inplace=inplace, 

806 alpha=alpha, 

807 allowed_dtypes=op.allowed, 

808 dtype_error=op.dtype_error, 

809 dtype_error_type=op.dtype_error_type, 

810 out_dtype_fn=op.out_dtype_fn, 

811 ) 

812 return None if inplace else res 

813 

814 

815def _apply_scalar(name: str, self, scalars, inplace: bool, alpha=1): 

816 """The ``.Scalar`` and ``.ScalarList`` overloads.""" 

817 op = BINARY_OPS[name] 

818 _log(name, "Scalar", inplace) 

819 if alpha != 1: 

820 for t in self: 

821 _check_alpha(alpha, t.dtype) 

822 allowed = op.allowed_scalar if op.allowed_scalar is not None else op.allowed 

823 res = foreach_binary_scalar( 

824 self, 

825 scalars, 

826 op.fn, 

827 inplace=inplace, 

828 alpha=alpha, 

829 allowed_dtypes=allowed, 

830 dtype_error=op.dtype_error, 

831 dtype_error_type=op.dtype_error_type, 

832 out_dtype_fn=op.out_dtype_fn, 

833 ) 

834 return None if inplace else res 

835 

836 

837def _apply_tensor(name: str, self, other: torch.Tensor, inplace: bool, alpha=1): 

838 """The ``.Tensor`` overload: one tensor broadcast across the whole list. 

839 

840 ATen accepts any shape here that broadcasts against each element of the list. 

841 A zero-dimensional tensor is the common case -- it is what optimizers pass -- 

842 and it is routed through the paired kernel with the operand read once per 

843 program rather than expanded into a full-size staging copy (or read back 

844 with ``.item()``). 

845 

846 Reading the value out would be simpler, but ``.item()`` synchronises the 

847 device: with sixteen kernels already queued it measured 2.11ms per call 

848 against PyTorch's 0.039ms, because every call drains the pipeline. Expanding 

849 instead keeps the scalar on the device and the launch asynchronous. 

850 """ 

851 if not isinstance(other, torch.Tensor): 

852 raise TypeError("argument 'other' must be a Tensor") 

853 op = BINARY_OPS[name] 

854 _log(name, "Tensor", inplace) 

855 self_list = list(self) 

856 if alpha != 1: 

857 for t in self_list: 

858 _check_alpha(alpha, t.dtype) 

859 if other.numel() == 1: 

860 # A single-element operand needs no copy at all: the kernel reads it 

861 # once per program as a uniform load, so the same tensor is handed to 

862 # every position and materialising it would only add a full-size copy. 

863 operands = [other] * len(self_list) 

864 scalar_operand = True 

865 else: 

866 operands = [ 

867 other if other.shape == t.shape else other.expand_as(t) for t in self_list 

868 ] 

869 scalar_operand = False 

870 # Promotion is resolved against the *original* operand, not the expanded 

871 # view: ATen treats a zero-dimensional tensor as a scalar here, so an fp16 

872 # list times an fp32 scalar tensor stays fp16, while a genuine fp32 tensor 

873 # list would promote. Expanding first and asking ``result_type`` afterwards 

874 # would silently widen the result. 

875 # 

876 # ``_promote_dtypes`` keys on (dtype, is-zero-dimensional) for each side, so 

877 # a list whose entries all share that pair resolves with one lookup rather 

878 # than sixteen. A mixed list falls back to the per-tensor form, which is 

879 # the same function and therefore yields the same dtypes. 

880 n = len(self_list) 

881 homogeneous = False 

882 if n: 

883 first = self_list[0] 

884 first_dtype = first.dtype 

885 first_zero_dim = first.dim() == 0 

886 homogeneous = True 

887 for t in self_list: 

888 if t.dtype is not first_dtype or (t.dim() == 0) != first_zero_dim: 

889 homogeneous = False 

890 break 

891 if homogeneous: 

892 promoted = _promote_dtypes(first, other) 

893 if op.out_dtype_fn is not None: 

894 promoted = op.out_dtype_fn(promoted) 

895 out_dtypes = [promoted] * n 

896 else: 

897 out_dtypes = [_promote_dtypes(t, other) for t in self_list] 

898 if op.out_dtype_fn is not None: 

899 out_dtypes = [op.out_dtype_fn(dt) for dt in out_dtypes] 

900 res = _flat_binary_list( 

901 self_list, 

902 operands, 

903 op.fn, 

904 inplace=inplace, 

905 alpha=alpha, 

906 allowed_dtypes=op.allowed, 

907 out_dtypes=out_dtypes, 

908 scalar_operand=scalar_operand, 

909 ) 

910 if res is _FLAT_FALLBACK: 

911 res = foreach_binary_list( 

912 self_list, 

913 operands, 

914 op.fn, 

915 inplace=inplace, 

916 alpha=alpha, 

917 allowed_dtypes=op.allowed, 

918 dtype_error=op.dtype_error, 

919 dtype_error_type=op.dtype_error_type, 

920 out_dtypes=out_dtypes, 

921 scalar_operand=scalar_operand, 

922 ) 

923 return None if inplace else res 

924 

925 

926def _apply_ternary(name: str, self, tensor1, tensor2, scalars, inplace: bool): 

927 """``addcmul`` / ``addcdiv``: three tensor lists and a value.""" 

928 op = BINARY_OPS[name] 

929 _log(name, "Ternary", inplace) 

930 # GCU400-specific fast path: the common foreach_ternary 2D grid exceeds the grid.y<=255 limit on large shapes; 

931 # when the fast-path prerequisites are not met, fall back to the common executor unchanged. 

932 if name == "addcdiv" and isinstance(scalars, torch.Tensor): 

933 fast_result = run_addcdiv_tensor(self, tensor1, tensor2, scalars, inplace) 

934 if fast_result is not _ADDC_DIV_FLAT_FALLBACK: 

935 return fast_result 

936 res = _flat_ternary( 

937 self, 

938 tensor1, 

939 tensor2, 

940 scalars, 

941 op.fn, 

942 inplace=inplace, 

943 allowed_dtypes=op.allowed, 

944 ) 

945 if res is _FLAT_FALLBACK: 

946 res = foreach_ternary( 

947 self, 

948 tensor1, 

949 tensor2, 

950 scalars, 

951 op.fn, 

952 inplace=inplace, 

953 allowed_dtypes=op.allowed, 

954 ) 

955 return None if inplace else res 

956 

957 

958# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- 

959# wrappers, one per registered ATen overload 

960# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- 

961# 

962# The bodies are uniform, so they are generated rather than typed sixty times; 

963# the module-level names below are what ``_FULL_CONFIG`` and the tests import, 

964# and each one is a distinct function object so a caplog probe can tell them 

965# apart. 

966 

967 

968def _make_list(name, inplace, with_alpha): 

969 if with_alpha: 

970 

971 def wrapper(self, other, *, alpha=1): 

972 return _apply_list(name, self, other, inplace, alpha) 

973 

974 else: 

975 

976 def wrapper(self, other): 

977 return _apply_list(name, self, other, inplace) 

978 

979 return wrapper 

980 

981 

982def _make_scalar(name, inplace, with_alpha): 

983 if with_alpha: 

984 

985 def wrapper(self, scalar, *, alpha=1): 

986 return _apply_scalar(name, self, scalar, inplace, alpha) 

987 

988 else: 

989 

990 def wrapper(self, scalar): 

991 return _apply_scalar(name, self, scalar, inplace) 

992 

993 return wrapper 

994 

995 

996def _make_tensor(name, inplace, with_alpha): 

997 if with_alpha: 

998 

999 def wrapper(self, other, *, alpha=1): 

1000 return _apply_tensor(name, self, other, inplace, alpha) 

1001 

1002 else: 

1003 

1004 def wrapper(self, other): 

1005 return _apply_tensor(name, self, other, inplace) 

1006 

1007 return wrapper 

1008 

1009 

1010def _make_ternary(name, inplace): 

1011 def wrapper(self, tensor1, tensor2, value=1): 

1012 return _apply_ternary(name, self, tensor1, tensor2, value, inplace) 

1013 

1014 return wrapper 

1015 

1016 

1017# ``alpha`` exists on the .List overload of add/sub and on add's .Tensor form 

1018# only; the other overloads reject it, so handing them the argument would accept 

1019# calls ATen refuses. Keyed by (operator, overload). 

1020_WITH_ALPHA = {("add", "List"), ("add", "Tensor"), ("sub", "List")} 

1021 

1022# Which overloads each operator actually has, from a live schema audit. Writing 

1023# this table by hand from the ATen names would risk registering a key that does 

1024# not exist (silently dead) or missing one that does. 

1025_OVERLOADS = { 

1026 "add": ("List", "Scalar", "ScalarList", "Tensor"), 

1027 "sub": ("List", "Scalar", "ScalarList"), 

1028 "mul": ("List", "Scalar", "ScalarList", "Tensor"), 

1029 "div": ("List", "Scalar", "ScalarList", "Tensor"), 

1030 "clamp_max": ("List", "Scalar", "ScalarList"), 

1031 "clamp_min": ("List", "Scalar", "ScalarList"), 

1032 "maximum": ("List", "Scalar", "ScalarList"), 

1033 "minimum": ("List", "Scalar", "ScalarList"), 

1034 "pow": ("List", "Scalar", "ScalarList"), 

1035} 

1036 

1037# ``lerp`` is ternary in *every* overload -- ``(self, tensors1, weight)`` where 

1038# only the weight varies between List / Scalar / ScalarList -- so it cannot use 

1039# the two-operand wrappers above and gets its own below. 

1040_LERP_OVERLOADS = ("List", "Scalar", "ScalarList") 

1041 

1042_globals = globals() 

1043 

1044for _name, _ovs in _OVERLOADS.items(): 

1045 for _inplace in (False, True): 

1046 _suffix = "_" if _inplace else "" 

1047 for _ov in _ovs: 

1048 _alpha = (_name, _ov) in _WITH_ALPHA 

1049 if _ov == "List": 

1050 _fn = _make_list(_name, _inplace, _alpha) 

1051 elif _ov == "Tensor": 

1052 _fn = _make_tensor(_name, _inplace, _alpha) 

1053 else: 

1054 _fn = _make_scalar(_name, _inplace, _alpha) 

1055 _attr = f"_foreach_{_name}{_suffix}_{_ov}" 

1056 _fn.__name__ = _attr 

1057 _fn.__qualname__ = _attr 

1058 _globals[_attr] = _fn 

1059 

1060for _name in ("addcmul", "addcdiv"): 

1061 for _inplace in (False, True): 

1062 _suffix = "_" if _inplace else "" 

1063 for _ov in ("Scalar", "ScalarList", "Tensor"): 

1064 _fn = _make_ternary(_name, _inplace) 

1065 _attr = f"_foreach_{_name}{_suffix}_{_ov}" 

1066 _fn.__name__ = _attr 

1067 _fn.__qualname__ = _attr 

1068 _globals[_attr] = _fn 

1069 

1070 

1071def _apply_lerp(self, tensors1, weight, inplace: bool): 

1072 """``self + weight * (tensors1 - self)``, weight per-list or per-tensor. 

1073 

1074 The ``List`` overload's weight is itself a TensorList, which the ternary 

1075 executor already handles by treating it as the third tensor operand; the 

1076 scalar forms broadcast their weight the same way ``addcmul``'s value does. 

1077 """ 

1078 op = BINARY_OPS["lerp"] 

1079 _log("lerp", "lerp", inplace) 

1080 if ( 

1081 isinstance(weight, (list, tuple)) 

1082 and weight 

1083 and isinstance(weight[0], torch.Tensor) 

1084 ): 

1085 # weights are tensors: fn(self, tensors1, weights, unused_scalar) 

1086 res = _flat_ternary( 

1087 self, 

1088 tensors1, 

1089 weight, 

1090 0.0, 

1091 _lerp_tensor_weight_fn, 

1092 inplace=inplace, 

1093 allowed_dtypes=op.allowed, 

1094 ) 

1095 if res is _FLAT_FALLBACK: 

1096 res = foreach_ternary( 

1097 self, 

1098 tensors1, 

1099 weight, 

1100 0.0, 

1101 _lerp_tensor_weight_fn, 

1102 inplace=inplace, 

1103 allowed_dtypes=op.allowed, 

1104 ) 

1105 else: 

1106 # GCU400-specific fast path: the common foreach_ternary 2D grid exceeds the grid.y<=255 limit on large shapes; 

1107 # when the fast-path prerequisites are not met, fall back to the common executor unchanged. 

1108 fast_result = run_lerp_scalar_list(self, tensors1, weight, inplace) 

1109 if fast_result is not _LERP_FLAT_FALLBACK: 

1110 return fast_result 

1111 res = _flat_ternary( 

1112 self, 

1113 tensors1, 

1114 tensors1, 

1115 weight, 

1116 _lerp_scalar_weight_fn, 

1117 inplace=inplace, 

1118 allowed_dtypes=op.allowed, 

1119 ) 

1120 if res is _FLAT_FALLBACK: 

1121 res = foreach_ternary( 

1122 self, 

1123 tensors1, 

1124 tensors1, 

1125 weight, 

1126 _lerp_scalar_weight_fn, 

1127 inplace=inplace, 

1128 allowed_dtypes=op.allowed, 

1129 ) 

1130 return None if inplace else res 

1131 

1132 

1133def _make_lerp(inplace): 

1134 def wrapper(self, tensors1, weight): 

1135 return _apply_lerp(self, tensors1, weight, inplace) 

1136 

1137 return wrapper 

1138 

1139 

1140for _inplace in (False, True): 

1141 _suffix = "_" if _inplace else "" 

1142 for _ov in _LERP_OVERLOADS: 

1143 _fn = _make_lerp(_inplace) 

1144 _attr = f"_foreach_lerp{_suffix}_{_ov}"

1200 family, which is why it cannot share the generated wrappers.

1212 exponent,

1214 _rpow_fn,

1217 dtype_error_type=op.dtype_error_type,

1240def registered_wrappers() -> Dict[str, Any]: 

1241 """Map ATen overload key -> wrapper, used by ``_FULL_CONFIG`` and tests. 

1242 

1243 Building the registration list from the same table that generated the 

1244 wrappers keeps the two from drifting: a wrapper with no key, or a key with 

1245 no wrapper, cannot happen by construction. 

1246 """ 

1247 out: Dict[str, Any] = {} 

1248 for name, ovs in _OVERLOADS.items(): 

1249 for inplace in (False, True): 

1250 suffix = "_" if inplace else "" 

1251 for ov in ovs: 

1252 out[f"_foreach_{name}{suffix}.{ov}"] = _globals[ 

1253 f"_foreach_{name}{suffix}_{ov}" 

1254 ] 

1255 for name in ("addcmul", "addcdiv"): 

1256 for inplace in (False, True): 

1257 suffix = "_" if inplace else "" 

1258 for ov in ("Scalar", "ScalarList", "Tensor"): 

1259 out[f"_foreach_{name}{suffix}.{ov}"] = _globals[ 

1260 f"_foreach_{name}{suffix}_{ov}" 

1261 ] 

1262 for inplace in (False, True): 

1263 suffix = "_" if inplace else "" 

1264 for ov in _LERP_OVERLOADS: 

1265 out[f"_foreach_lerp{suffix}.{ov}"] = _globals[f"_foreach_lerp{suffix}_{ov}"] 

1266 out["_foreach_copy"] = _foreach_copy 

1267 out["_foreach_copy_"] = _foreach_copy_ 

1268 out["_foreach_pow.ScalarAndTensor"] = _foreach_pow_ScalarAndTensor 

1269 return out
